[[Colo-Colo]] won their thirty-second title following a 3–0 away win at [[Huachipato]] on 9 December.{{cite web|url=https://www.publimetro.cl/cl/grafico-chile/2017/12/09/colo-colo-huachipato-final.html|title=Colo Colo se sacó la mufa, no arrugó y es el flamante campeón del fútbol chileno|date=9 December 2017|work=publimetro.cl|language=es|access-date=12 December 2017}} [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] were the defending champions. ==Format changes== Starting in 2017, the [[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|ANFP]] approved a change from the European calendar season (July–May) that had been used since 2013 to a calendar year season (February–December).{{cite web |url=http://www.emol.com/noticias/Deportes/2016/04/01/795915/Se-terminara-el-torneo-a-la-europea-del-futbol-chileno-y-el-2017-se-jugara-de-febrero-a-diciembre.html|title=Se terminará el torneo "estilo europeo" del fútbol chileno y el 2017 se jugará de febrero a diciembre |language=es |publisher=Emol.com |date=1 April 2016 |access-date=28 May 2017 }} The year calendar would have been implemented for the 2017 season, however, it was postponed for one year. In order to manage this transition, the 2017 Clausura tournament, part of the 2016–17 season, was followed up by a single championship in the second semester of the year. The [[2018 Chilean Primera División|2018 season]] will be played as a single tournament, without the Apertura-Clausura system.{{cite web|url=http://www.latercera.com/noticia/2018-vuelve-torneo-largo/|title=El 2018 vuelve el torneo largo|publisher=latercera.com|language=es}} ==Teams== ===Stadia and locations=== {{location map+ |Chile |float=right |width=300 |caption=Locations of the 2017 Chilean Primera División teams. |places= {{location map~ |Chile |lat=-34.983333|long=-71.233333|label=
